question: The famous "Katra" mound in Mathura is known for remains of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Temples and monasteries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Katra mound**, also known as **Katra Keshavdev**, is a prominent archaeological site located in **Mathura**, **Uttar Pradesh**. It is widely recognized for housing the remains of ancient **temples and monasteries**.
 
• Excavations at this site were initiated as early as the **19th century** by **Alexander Cunningham**, the founder of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, who identified it as a site of immense historical and religious significance.
 
• The mound has provided structural evidence of the **Yasha Vihara**, a famous **Buddhist monastery** that flourished during the **Gupta period** (**4th to 6th century AD**).
 
• Archaeological findings at the site confirm that it was a major center for the **Mathura School of Art**, yielding numerous sculptures made of **spotted red sandstone**.
